headline: High-risk editor-to-agent interaction: Cursor’s filesystem/MCP/write defaults can conflict with LightZero’s read-only, non-networked profile, while compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default, so attacker-controlled content can reach its agent loop. LightZero has no input surfaces or tool use, so it is not itself a bridge, but the pair still has a plausible shared-filesystem/manual-copy path via Cursor. Uncertainty about undocumented interaction keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Cursor opens a file or clipboard text containing adversarial instructions, the agent loop may follow them.
IF the two agents are bridged by manual copy-paste or shared workspace files, injected text can propagate.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based ingestion for the session.
Keep LightZero outputs out of Cursor-opened files.
Use a separate workspace directory per agent.
Review any MCP server provenance before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files and open buffers and may send content to model providers; LightZero reads nothing and writes nothing, so leakage is one-way from Cursor rather than mutual. Because Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, a shared workspace can expose sensitive material even though LightZero itself is inert. The shared filesystem path makes medium the safest choice.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Cursor’s workspace, they can be included in model context.
IF Cursor is configured to send file contents to external providers, those contents may leave the machine.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace.
Open only the minimum files needed in Cursor.
Disable network access for the session if feasible.
Use separate OS users or directories per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has broad write, shell, and git capabilities, while LightZero has no filesystem, network, or subprocess capabilities. That means there is little direct write-write conflict; the main risk is Cursor mutating shared files that LightZero merely consumes. Because LightZero cannot write back, overlap is limited and blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, Cursor can change files LightZero later reads.
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode, it may modify shared state without coordination.
mitigations: Avoid a shared git checkout.
Run Cursor with approval mode, not Yolo mode.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Use file locks for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or edits that LightZero does not verify, but LightZero has no action-taking authority or downstream write path. The pair therefore lacks the high-risk pattern where one agent’s output directly triggers irreversible actions. The main issue is unverified handoff from Cursor to a passive consumer, which is limited but real.
conditions: IF Cursor’s generated edits are copied into a workflow without review, errors can propagate.
IF LightZero is used as a downstream evaluator of Cursor output, it will not independently verify facts.
mitigations: Require human review before applying Cursor edits.
Do not treat Cursor output as authoritative.
Keep LightZero isolated from any action-taking pipeline.
Add a checksum or diff review step.
requires-engineering: build verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor’s docs indicate handling of source code, open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider API keys, while LightZero’s profile shows no data classes touched and no network or storage surfaces. There is no evidence of a residency or regulated-data mismatch between the pair, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary code-handling hygiene rather than a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor’s workspace, it may be processed by external model providers.
IF the operator stores secrets in open files, Cursor may surface them during assistance.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Review provider privacy settings before use.
Limit clipboard use for sensitive material.
requires-engineering: add data-class policy enforcement.
